Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph shows a complete white-out of the right hemithorax with a contralateral (leftward) mediastinal shift, which is the classic presentation of a massive pleural effusion pushing structures away from the affected side. Options suggesting atelectasis or pneumothorax are incorrect because atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift and pneumothorax would appear radiolucent (black), not opaque.
